"**Dance Monkey**" is a song by Australian singer [Tones and I](Tones_and_I "Tones and I"), released on 10 May 2019 as the second single (first in the US) from Tones and I's debut EP *[The Kids Are Coming](The_Kids_Are_Coming "The Kids Are Coming")*. The song was produced and mixed by [Konstantin Kersting](Konstantin_Kersting "Konstantin Kersting").[[3]](Dance_Monkey#cite_note-3)

"Dance Monkey" topped the official singles charts in over 38 countries and peaked within the top ten of many others, including the United States. The song broke the record for the most weeks at number one on the Australian singles chart at 24 non-consecutive weeks.[[4]](Dance_Monkey#cite_note-4) It also broke the record for the most weeks spent at the top of the [UK Singles Chart](UK_Singles_Chart "UK Singles Chart") by a female artist with 11 weeks at the top. When it hit number four in the US, it became the first top-five hit solely written by a woman in over eight years.[[5]](Dance_Monkey#cite_note-5) On Spotify, as of June 2023, the song was the [most streamed by a female artist](Top_spotify_songs "Top spotify songs") and the third-most overall, with over 2.8 billion streams.

The song has received a number of awards. It won [Best Pop Release](ARIA_Award_for_Best_Pop_Release "ARIA Award for Best Pop Release") at the [ARIA Music Awards of 2019](ARIA_Music_Awards_of_2019 "ARIA Music Awards of 2019"),[[6]](Dance_Monkey#cite_note-ARIA_noms_2019-6) Song of the Year at the [APRA Music Awards of 2020](APRA_Music_Awards_of_2020 "APRA Music Awards of 2020")[[7]](Dance_Monkey#cite_note-apra-7) and Independent Song of the Year at the [AIR Awards of 2020](AIR_Awards_of_2020 "AIR Awards of 2020").[[8]](Dance_Monkey#cite_note-2020wins-8) It was also the Grand Prize winner of the 2019 International Songwriting Competition.[[9]](Dance_Monkey#cite_note-international_songwriting-9)

## Lyrics

When interviewed by DJ Smallzy in July 2019 on Australian radio station Nova FM, Tones explained that Dance Monkey's lyrics are about the relationship she had with her audience when she was [busking](Busking "Busking") (street performing) on the streets of Australia:

"I wrote this song when I was busking, and about the pressure that I felt to always be entertaining people on the street. And if they didn't like it, when they looked at their phones they could just click something else; ... we are all so used to being entertained at the click of a button."

"So when you're [busking] on the street, .. to command [your] attention, people would be like: 'again! again!' .. 'more! more!' .. or they would just leave.
